clue.text: Draws one, a parasitic plant

parts.note: raffles are prize draws, lotteries for donated prizes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lottery winner turns out to be a plant that lives off others.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafflesia is a genus of Southeast Asian plants that feed on vines and produce huge flowers.

clue.text: Not as common in cellar are rats

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words cellar are rats, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A cellar's rats are a less frequent sight than one might fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, so it means less common or less frequently found.

clue.text: Patsy to come down and stay

explanation.walkthrough: A guy rope is a stay, the nautical word for a supporting line.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a person easily blamed or cheated, a scapegoat or dupe.

clue.text: One watching what is said?

parts.note: said things are normally heard, but this person follows speech by watching the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads lips understands speech by watching the speaker's mouth movements.

clue.text: Series of person-to-person meetings in career, going back

explanation.definitionFit: At a speed-dating event, singles hold a sequence of short one-to-one conversations with potential partners.

clue.text: Tune from musical husband's forgotten

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
h is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man has failed to remember a song from a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody, a simple tune.

clue.text: Sketch includes cheerleader's behind in ra-ra?

indicators.note: the sketch takes the other letter inside itself

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

indicators.note: the behind of a word is its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: A ra-ra skirt is the short flounced skirt worn by cheerleaders; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A ra-ra is a short frilled skirt of the kind cheerleaders wear, so it is one example.

clue.text: Stern almost split

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: stern and severe both mean harsh and strict

explanation.surface: A harsh rebuke nearly causes a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to cut or split it apart.

clue.text: Soldier taken over impressive base

indicators.note: in a down clue taken over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: GI is the usual name for an American soldier
noble can mean grand or impressive

explanation.surface: A soldier is captured by a grand military station.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in its moral sense means low and dishonourable.

clue.text: Wealthy globetrotters on a 747?

parts.note: rich travellers are pictured literally as a group set aboard a jumbo jet

explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are the rich fashionable people who fly between glamorous places.

clue.text: Runs slip away, resulting in setback to recovery

parts.note: r is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
time is said to elapse when it slips away

explanation.surface: A batter scores runs but time slips by and the comeback stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is falling ill again after seeming to get better.

clue.text: Income on location

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a venue is the place where something happens

explanation.surface: Earnings depend on where you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially the money a business or government takes in.

clue.text: Scoundrel's accent, not British

indicators.note: not means the named letter is excluded

parts.note: a brogue is a strong regional accent, typically Irish

explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal or villain.

clue.text: Pleasing tavern back in Leeds I used

indicators.note: the turned tavern is put inside the rearranged letters
used means worn or knocked about, so these letters get reworked
back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a bar is a tavern or pub

explanation.walkthrough: 'used' reworks LEEDSI into DESILE; 'back' turns BAR into RAB, which goes 'in' to give DESI-RAB-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desirable is attractive and worth having, so it pleases.

clue.text: Petrified stinking cedars, rigid

indicators.note: stinking suggests something rotten or bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: rigid and stiff both mean unbending

explanation.surface: Fossilised trees, smelly cedars, have turned hard as stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stinking' turns CEDARS into SCARED; petrified trees have literally turned to stone, the surface trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified in the sense of terrified, too frightened to move.

clue.text: Tell, for example

definitions.meaning: to tell someone something is to state it
... introduces an example, as in a fruit, ..., an apple

explanation.definitionFit: Say means to tell or state, and also serves as an informal for instance.

clue.text: Hooter goes at end of excellent annual championship game

indicators.note: the bird is placed after the word for excellent

parts.note: superb means excellent
an owl is a bird that hoots

explanation.surface: A horn sounds at the end of a terrific yearly title match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Super Bowl is the American football championship final, played every year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the NFL's yearly title match.

clue.text: These people act overemotionally in play NY borough put on

parts.note: a drama is a play
Queens is one of the five boroughs of New York City

explanation.surface: Histrionic performers are staging a show in a New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama queens are people who overreact theatrically to everything.

clue.text: Out of bed compiling crosswords? That could be worrying

crossword compilers are called setters, and their work setting

clue.text: They appear to be powerful, but they're not good during rows on daily

explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts PAPER before TIGERS; rows here are tiers, not quarrels, though the surface invites the quarrel sense.

clue.text: Large company stocking Italian wine — you need credit cards

parts.note: PLC is a public limited company in Britain
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: A big firm stocks Italian wine and asks customers to pay by card.
explanation.walkthrough: PLC is the British suffix for a public limited company.

clue.text: Snaffle coin

definitions.meaning: a snaffle is a simple mouthpiece for a horse's bridle
a ... is a small coin, as in a threepenny ...

explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a type of mouthpiece on a bridle, and a small coin was called a bit.

clue.text: A bitter cocktail — it may go to a cardinal's head

definitions.text: it may go to a cardinal's head

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mix, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sharp mixed drink might go straight to a churchman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes ABITTER into the answer; the surface suggests the drink goes to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by clergy, scarlet for a cardinal.

clue.text: Footballer strangely angry about performance against foremost of sides

indicators.note: against means next to, so the letter is set beside
the rearranged letters go about, around, the performance word

explanation.walkthrough: 'against' here means next to, not opposed to. Ryan Giggs is a Welsh former Manchester United winger, famous for a long career at the club.

clue.text: Accepted going topless is a sin

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter goes

parts.note: agreed means accepted

explanation.surface: It is generally accepted that baring all is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: To the point, language used at conclusion of summit

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Diplomats speak briefly at the end of a summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and concise, sticking to the point.

clue.text: Take great risks over capturing large Spanish hero

indicators.note: capturing means holding the letter inside
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to dice with death is to take great risks

explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DICE into ECID, and 'capturing' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was the medieval Castilian warrior celebrated as Spain's national hero.

clue.text: Active and energetic, one got working around hospital

clue.text: What may be extracted from half of olives treated?

clue.text: Senseless, one point about one in charge

I is the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Top copper put back inside — that's easy to understand

clue.text: Figure lad swimming? I'll help him, if floundering!

definitions.text: Figure lad swimming? I'll help him, if floundering!

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement in water, so the letters move into a new order
